stumbles.quote: On 2026-11-09, Oskar asked, "does that mean we could trim these to 256 length vectors without penalty by reversing the widening?"
stumbles.why: Oskar is never introduced, and the question refers to an earlier conversation and a "widening" that the text doesn't explain.

stumbles.quote: Folding Ettin-17m's final 256-to-768 output matrix into a 256-to-256 matrix
stumbles.why: It doesn't say what the matrix is or why a 256-to-768 projection can be folded this way. A 256-to-256 matrix can't be derived from it without more explanation.

stumbles.quote: quantized to smaller, more accurate remex codes
stumbles.why: "remex" is never explained. "More accurate" is unclear, because 3-bit codes at 256 dimensions score 0.868 against 0.857 for the live index, and that is measured against float search.

stumbles.quote: the live index uses 2-bit remex codes across 768 dimensions
stumbles.why: "The live index" is not defined. The text also doesn't say which index this is, and it later says site indexes stay 768-dimensional.

stumbles.quote: Remex's rotation also folds into that 256-to-256 matrix so the model emits rotated coordinates directly; with an int8 head, 4-bit codes reach 0.931.
stumbles.why: The rotation and the "int8 head" are unexplained. It's unclear whether the 0.931 result includes the fold, and what it should be compared with.

stumbles.quote: The List Scout page now runs the folded 256-dimensional model, producing identical classifier answers and cutting fitting time from 3.6 s to 1.2 s.
stumbles.why: "List Scout" and its classifier are never introduced, and "fitting time" is unexplained. The text doesn't say what was fitted.

stumbles.quote: without loss in float search, and quantized to smaller, more accurate remex codes by using 3 or 4 bits per dimension
stumbles.why: The claim says "3 or 4 bits" are more accurate. The 3-bit result is only slightly better (0.868 against 0.857), and 256-dimensional 2-bit is worse, so the claim is easy to misread.

point: Ettin-17m embeddings can be folded down to 256 dimensions with no change in float search, and 3- or 4-bit remex codes at 256 dimensions beat the current 2-bit 768-dimensional index in fewer bytes, though many terms go unexplained.
